text:
Help me answer my landlord. I own a 40-seat Vietnamese restaurant, and my 5-year lease ends in August. He wants to raise the rent from $4,800 a month to $5,650, which is about 18%.

Facts:
- I've been in the space for 10 years, over two leases.
- I paid rent late twice in early 2024, by 11 days and by 19 days. He waived the late fees both times. I've paid on time every month since.
- I put about $70,000 into the kitchen in 2019, including a new hood system that stays with the building.
- The empty unit two doors down has been for lease for 14 months at $28 a square foot a year. His number works out to about $29 for my space.
- I can pay $5,100 a month if I get a 5-year lease, with 3% increases each year after the first.
- He told me a coffee chain asked about my space.

Keep it short and polite, under 300 words.

I left the late payments out of the letter on purpose. He already knows about them, and bringing them up makes them look bigger than they are. I also didn't write that you've "always" paid on time, because he could easily point out that's not true. If he raises it, you can say you've paid on time every month since early 2024.

<final_document>
Dear [Landlord's name],

Thank you for sending the renewal terms. I've valued our relationship over the past ten years, and I'd like to keep [Restaurant name] in your building for a long time to come.

I've thought carefully about the proposed $5,650. That's about an 18% increase, which is more than I can take on in one step. I'd like to propose this instead:

- **A new 5-year lease starting at $5,100 per month**
- **3% annual increases after the first year**

That's a meaningful raise right away, and by the fifth year the rent would be about $5,740, higher than the figure you proposed. You would also have a committed tenant for five more years.

A few things I hope you'll consider:

- **Stability.** We've been here a decade and have built a loyal customer base on this block.
- **Investment in the space.** In 2019 I put about $70,000 into the kitchen, including the new hood system that stays with the building.
- **The current market.** The unit two doors down has been listed at $28 per square foot for over a year without a tenant. Your proposal comes to about $29 for my space, and a vacancy of any length would cost us both.

I understand you've had interest from other businesses, and I respect that you have options. I'm hoping we can find terms that work well for both of us.

I'd be glad to meet and talk it through whenever it suits you.

Best regards,
[Your name]
[Restaurant name]
[Phone]
</final_document>

The letter is about 270 words. Before you send it, check that $5,650 really does come to about $29 per square foot for your space, since the letter relies on that comparison.
